conclusions.result: Public canonical rotate requires auth_pool; no optional or permissive fallback remains. The internal writer receives the same dependency.

Presented token hash drives the existing token/family lookup with FOR UPDATE OF t,f. user_id is read from that locked token row, then bound to account_legacy_fenced_v1; request body/cookie subject fields do not supply the fenced identity.
Existing FamilyRevoked rollback/return stays before auth lookup, so already-revoked families do not require a successful new fence query. No new write precedes that existing return.

Mandatory restricted projection query executes before absolute-TTL revocation, reuse revocation, expired-token revocation, replacement insertion, used/replaced_by mutation and audit insertion. A committed fence returns InvalidToken after rollback, preserving existing refusal semantics.

Nonoptional bool decoding makes SQL NULL an error. Connection/query/decoding errors propagate as AuthError::Sqlx and public rotate converts non-Refresh errors to constant Storage. Query-error unwinding drops the uncommitted SQLx transaction; no credential or audit write has occurred at that point.

Actual HTTP route passes retained state.auth_database or returns Storage; existing cookie-over-body precedence chooses the actual presented token before canonical rotation. Access-token, JSON refresh-token and Set-Cookie construction remain after successful rotation.

Unchanged production composition root authenticates console_auth_rt, validates serving-role connection identities and equal observed database target against the business pool, then retains it in AuthRestState. This review does not infer equivalent validation for arbitrary manually constructed PgPool callers.
Existing mapping emits401 for InvalidToken/FamilyRevoked and500 for constant Storage. No SQL driver detail, DSN or raw token is exposed through the added error path.

concurrency_and_scope_limits: Guarantee covers a fence committed before the separate auth query. It does not serialize a concurrent Account activation/cutover with the legacy business transaction; source explicitly requires admission pause and drain.

Token and family row locks serialize legacy rotations and remain held during the auth lookup. Production uses a distinct two-connection auth pool with three-second acquisition timeout; this is not a measured throughput bound or proof of SQL execution deadline.

Passing one PgPool as both transaction and auth pool can require two simultaneous connections per rotation; caller-owned small/saturated shared pools may wait or return Storage. Production composition uses separate pools; saturation testing was not performed.
Credential/family/audit mutation refusal is proven by the selected tests. Existing earlier HTTP rate-limit accounting and transaction-local tenant GUC setup are not claimed to be absent.

pre_mortem: A request-selected subject, HTTP-only guard, query error treated as absence, postwrite denial or missing auth dependency could let fenced legacy refresh mutate material. Locked-token identity, mandatory canonical prewrite query, nonoptional bool/error mapping and six genuine before/after effect controls address those cases.
